subject: Comparing parameters from different regression models?

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Comparing parameters from different regression models?
parts:
Hello,

I used two ways to estimate regression weights:
a) a hierarchical model with post stratification
b) an ordinary/non-hierarchical regression 

Now I would like to compare the regression weights 
obtained by these two methods.

Currently I am using a Bayesian bootstrap to do this,
but I am unsure if I am doing this right or if I should 
use a different method altogether.

My specific questions are:

1) Which method would you recommend?
2) For the Bayesian bootstrap: Should I  for each 
    bootstrap sample 
- first calculate the weighted mean/median for each 
  parameter and then calculated the ratio 
  (or difference) or
- first select random samples from the
  posteriors, then calculate the element wise 
  ratio, and finally calculate the mean/median 
  of that ratio
- something entirely different?

I'd appreciate any pointer to relevant literature, my 
own literature search has been without success 
so far.


Best - Guido


PS:
At first I just took a large random sample 
(with replacement) from each posterior and simply
calculated the element wise ratio to get a posterior
distribution of ratios. However, these posteriors are 
not easy to deal with, because when parameter values
get close to zero ratios become very large.

messages.subject: Re: Comparing parameters from different regression models?
parts:
I am trying to resurrect this thread with a shorter question:

I used two ways to estimate regression coefficients:
a) a hierarchical model with post-stratification
b) a non-hierarchical regression without post-stratification

Would anybody have an idea what the best way is to compare the regression coefficients for the same predictor from the two models?
I would like to get the difference and the ratio of the posteriors (with the associated highest density intervals).

Thanks in advance - Guido

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Comparing parameters from different regression models?
parts:
Does the post-stratification affect the coefficients?

What do you want to compare? You can compute the
posterior of the difference (assuming independent fits)
with subtraction assuming you have the same number of draws
in both samples. And then you can use those to compute
whatever event probabilities you want.

Stan doesn't calculate highest density intervals, so you'll need
another package for that. Andrew was involved with SPIn,
but I've never used it:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/SPIn/index.html

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Comparing parameters from different regression models?
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply Bob!

Post stratification (which I do outside stan) does effect the coefficients,
but the differences do not seem to be very strong. 

Computing the differences has worked well. Ratios proved more difficult 
because the posterior of some coefficients are centered around 0, 
which results in posteriors with a very large variance (because the two 
samples can be either both positive, both negative, or positive and negative).

Now I thought about estimating the ratios in another hierarchical model
(where the data would be the posteriors from the original model) to deal
with the very large variances.

Do you think this makes sense?

Guido


PS: I did know about SPI, I used HDInterval: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/HDInterval/index.html

> On May 30, 2016, at 10:52 AM, Guido Biele <guido...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks for the quick reply Bob!
>
> Post stratification (which I do outside stan) does effect the coefficients,
> but the differences do not seem to be very strong.
>
> Computing the differences has worked well. Ratios proved more difficult
> because the posterior of some coefficients are centered around 0,
> which results in posteriors with a very large variance (because the two
> samples can be either both positive, both negative, or positive and negative).

Ratios are problematic for exactly the reasons you mention.
Usually with both positive and negative values, they don't make
sense.

> Now I thought about estimating the ratios in another hierarchical model
> (where the data would be the posteriors from the original model) to deal
> with the very large variances.
>
> Do you think this makes sense?

You haven't said what you want to do this for, so it's hard to say.

Usually it's a better idea to just make a joint model
than try to fiddle posteriors into priors.

- Bob
